text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Juri Ott, head of the central (Old Town) district of Tallinn was excluded from the city government at the mayor's request, officially as part of the adjustment of the city government membership. But Ott has been linked to a corruption scandal concerning the privatisation of apartments.

- Russian Metropolitan Cyril visited Estonia, informed the prime minister about negotiations with Constantinople and asked the Estonian authorities to register the Russia-oriented Orthodox church as the Estonian Orthodox Church.

- A hunger strike of six workers at the bankrupt Oru peat processing plant in northeast Estonia began. Protesters are demanding the payment of six months of wages withheld by the firm. They also demand that the liquidation of the plant be prevented to maintain the only employer in the area.
- The security police has approved the publication of the first seven names of former Soviet secret police KGB informers and collaborators.
- The author Valentin Kuik won the first award of the Estonian Novels Foundation contest.
- A survey commissioned by the agriculture ministry shows that 75 percent of buyers welcome the "Buy Estonian" principle and live according to it.
- Parliament formed a European affairs commission to advance integration with Europe at a parliamentary level.
- Documents give grounds for suspicions that the repair of private apartments of Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi and Savings Bank director Olari Taal were made with municipal funds, the newspaper alleges.
- Environment Minister Villu Reiljan has violated the law by allowing the leasing of cars using Environment Foundation money.
- The bankruptcy of the Oru peat plant threatens the contract of three turf briquette firms with a Swedish buyer.
- The number of tourists visiting Estonia has increased again after a decrease in the recent years; last year's growth was partly caused by the return of Russian tourists.
